topics.topic: Existing witness check bound to the CLK-002 Required tests
questions: Which existing witness check is bound to the CLK-002 Required tests?
Which existing witness check is bound to the CLK-002 Required tests item and asserts CLK-002?
Which existing check is bound to CLK-002 and will assert its source-check, counting-wall-clock, expiry-boundary, and elapsed-clock obligations?

quotes: - Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal].
judgement.why: The exhaustive witness line binds both existing checks to CLK-001 and therefore answers that no existing witness check is bound to CLK-002.

topics.topic: Required verification coverage for CLK-002 clock-count and elapsed-clock restrictions
questions: What tests show the clock-count rule for all remaining time-dependent operations, that the audit writer takes exactly its one permitted further reading, and that elapsed readings are never converted to instants or compared with persisted records?
What required check demonstrates that the elapsed reading is never converted to an instant, compared or ordered against persisted timestamps, or retained anywhere outside the A25 in-memory window?

quotes:
- CLK-002: the clock source is the only reader of the host's wall and
  elapsed clocks; an operation takes one wall reading, and that instant
  decides every current-time comparison it makes and every portal-owned
  timestamp it writes (the audit writer's reading of `occurred_at` aside);
  the elapsed clock is read once per viewer-entry request,
  only to measure the A25 rate-limit window, and its reading is kept only
  in that window's in-memory state, never persisted, turned into an instant or ordered against a persisted record.

- CLK-002: a source check that no module other than the clock source calls
  a host clock (`datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `datetime.today`,
  `date.today`, `time.time`, `time.monotonic` and their variants); a test
  per time-dependent operation (authentication of a session or credential,
  revocation cascades, activation, bootstrap) with a counting wall-clock
  source that the operation takes exactly one wall reading, apart from the
  audit writer's, and that an expiry equal to that reading is refused while
  the timestamps it writes equal that reading; and a viewer-entry test with a counting clock source that one request takes
  exactly one elapsed reading, that the window decision at its boundary
  follows that reading, and that no record written by the request holds
  it.
judgement.divergence: One verifier checks only the enumerated wall-clock operations and that viewer entry writes no elapsed value to a record; another also counts the audit writer and every remaining time-dependent operation and detects conversion, comparison, ordering, or retention of elapsed readings, so the owner sees the same implementation pass one suite and fail the other.
judgement.why: The Required tests do not say how to demonstrate the audit writer's permitted reading count or the prohibitions on converting, ordering, comparing, or retaining elapsed readings outside the window.

witness.initial: A portal implementation takes two wall readings while appending one audit record and converts the viewer-entry elapsed reading into a transient instant without persisting it.
events: A verification author implements exactly the named counting tests and checks only that the viewer-entry request writes no elapsed reading to a record.
Another verification author adds checks for the audit writer's count and for transient conversion or comparison of the elapsed reading.
The two suites run against the same implementation.
outcomes: The first suite passes because the named operations satisfy their counts and no written record contains the elapsed reading.
The second suite fails because the audit writer reads twice and the elapsed reading is converted outside the A25 window.
basis:
- CLK-002: a source check that no module other than the clock source calls
  a host clock (`datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `datetime.today`,
  `date.today`, `time.time`, `time.monotonic` and their variants); a test
  per time-dependent operation (authentication of a session or credential,
  revocation cascades, activation, bootstrap) with a counting wall-clock
  source that the operation takes exactly one wall reading, apart from the
  audit writer's, and that an expiry equal to that reading is refused while
  the timestamps it writes equal that reading; and a viewer-entry test with a counting clock source that one request takes
  exactly one elapsed reading, that the window decision at its boundary
  follows that reading, and that no record written by the request holds
  it.

topics.topic: Whether a deploy may retry an incomplete vulnerability check or requires a new deploy
questions: After that one check cannot complete, can the same waiting deploy retry and eventually start, or can it proceed only through a new deploy with a new single check?
After a transient OSV failure, may the waiting deploy retry OSV and start when that retry passes, or is any retry a new deploy because each deploy makes only one check?

quotes:
A check that cannot
   complete does not pass, and the deploy waits. Each deploy makes one
   check, and its verdict on the OSV data it read decides that deploy; an
   advisory added, changed or withdrawn after that read is judged by the
   next deploy.
judgement.divergence: One deployment procedure retries the incomplete check within the waiting deploy and starts the service after a passing retry; another treats the failed attempt as the deploy's single check and requires the operator to initiate a new deploy, which the operator and users notice as different recovery and availability.
judgement.why: The text does not decide whether retrying an incomplete check remains the one check of the waiting deploy or constitutes the next deploy.

witness.initial: A built image is ready and has no known vulnerable distribution, but OSV is temporarily unreachable.
events: The deployment operator starts the deploy.
Its OSV check cannot complete, so the deploy waits.
OSV becomes reachable without an image change or a new deploy request.
outcomes: The waiting deploy retries the check, obtains a passing verdict, and starts the service.
The waiting deploy cannot perform another check, so it remains stopped until the operator initiates a new deploy.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users observing service availability
basis: A deploy is the start of the service from a built image.

topics.topic: Whether clock-independent operations take one wall-clock reading or none
questions: Must an operation that writes no timestamp and makes no current-time comparison take one wall-clock reading, or take none?
Must an operation that writes no timestamp and makes no current-time comparison still take exactly one wall-clock reading, or must it take none?

judgement.why: This is the same question about wall-clock readings by clock-independent operations, and the cited texts have not changed since P2.

precedent.topic: Required wall-clock reading count for operations that do not use current time
quotes:
- **Time.** Only `system_clock` reads the host clocks (A28). An operation
  that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses
  it; the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry
  window from it. No other module reads a host clock.
precedent.why: The later module rule limits the wall reading to an operation that needs the current instant, so an operation with no timestamp or current-time comparison takes none.

topics.topic: Host-clock calls and access patterns rejected by the CLK-002 source check
questions: What exact calls and access patterns must the source check reject as host-clock variants?

quotes:
- CLK-002: a source check that no module other than the clock source calls
  a host clock (`datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `datetime.today`,
  `date.today`, `time.time`, `time.monotonic` and their variants); a test
  per time-dependent operation (authentication of a session or credential,
  revocation cascades, activation, bootstrap) with a counting wall-clock
  source that the operation takes exactly one wall reading, apart from the
  audit writer's, and that an expiry equal to that reading is refused while
  the timestamps it writes equal that reading; and a viewer-entry test with a counting clock source that one request takes
  exactly one elapsed reading, that the window decision at its boundary
  follows that reading, and that no record written by the request holds
  it.
judgement.divergence: One source-check implementation rejects any equivalent host-clock access such as `time.perf_counter()` or an aliased/native wrapper, while another rejects only calls matching the enumerated names; the verification operator sees the same source fail or pass.
judgement.why: The phrase “and their variants” leaves the source check's rejected APIs, aliases, wrappers, and equivalent host-clock access patterns undefined.

witness.initial: A module other than the clock source calls `time.perf_counter()` to make a duration-based decision.
events: A source check limited to the explicitly enumerated function names scans the module.
A source check treating equivalent elapsed-clock APIs as variants scans the same module.
outcomes: The name-limited check passes the module.
The semantic check fails the module because it reads a host elapsed clock outside the clock source.
basis:
- CLK-002: a source check that no module other than the clock source calls
  a host clock (`datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `datetime.today`,
  `date.today`, `time.time`, `time.monotonic` and their variants); a test
  per time-dependent operation (authentication of a session or credential,
  revocation cascades, activation, bootstrap) with a counting wall-clock
  source that the operation takes exactly one wall reading, apart from the
  audit writer's, and that an expiry equal to that reading is refused while
  the timestamps it writes equal that reading; and a viewer-entry test with a counting clock source that one request takes
  exactly one elapsed reading, that the window decision at its boundary
  follows that reading, and that no record written by the request holds

topics.topic: Single OSV advisory-data cutoff for a multi-distribution deploy check
questions: What single OSV-data cutoff governs a deploy when advisory data changes while the check is reading results for multiple installed distributions?

quotes:
Before it,
   every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read in that
   same deploy; no earlier verdict or advisory copy is reused.

Each deploy makes one
   check, and its verdict on the OSV data it read decides that deploy; an
   advisory added, changed or withdrawn after that read is judged by the
   next deploy.
judgement.divergence: One checker treats each distribution's query time as its advisory cutoff, so query order can let the image start; another uses one deploy-wide advisory snapshot or cutoff and blocks the same image, which the deployment operator and waiting users notice.
judgement.why: The text refers to one read and one deploy verdict but does not define a deploy-wide cutoff when OSV data is fetched at different times for multiple distributions.

witness.initial: A built image contains distributions A and B, and OSV initially has no advisory affecting either installed version.
events: The deployment check queries OSV for A.
OSV publishes a non-withdrawn advisory affecting A's installed version.
The check queries OSV for B and decides whether to start the image.
outcomes: A per-distribution cutoff treats A as clean because it was queried before publication, so the image passes and starts.
A deploy-wide cutoff that includes the advisory blocks the image in this deploy.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users waiting for the service
basis:
A deploy is the start of the service from a built image. Before it,
   every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read in that
   same deploy; no earlier verdict or advisory copy is reused.

Each deploy makes one
   check, and its verdict on the OSV data it read decides that deploy; an
   advisory added, changed or withdrawn after that read is judged by the
   next deploy.

topics.topic: Whether A25 rate limiting may compare elapsed time instead of wall-clock instants
questions: Is the A25 viewer-entry rate-limit comparison an exception to the rule that the wall-clock instant decides every current-time comparison?

quotes:
- the elapsed clock gives a duration scale: one reading per viewer-entry
  request of a clock that cannot move backwards, in seconds as a float, the same value
  `time.monotonic()` gives. It measures the viewer-entry rate-limit window of
  A25 only; a reading is kept only in that window's in-memory state, never
  written to a persisted record, never turned into an instant and never
  ordered against a persisted record.

and a viewer-entry test with a counting clock source that one request takes
  exactly one elapsed reading, that the window decision at its boundary
  follows that reading, and that no record written by the request holds
  it.
judgement.why: The text explicitly makes the A25 window a duration-scale decision whose boundary follows the elapsed reading, rather than a current-instant comparison against persisted time.

topics.topic: Whether dependency security review covers all resolved distributions or only direct pins
questions: Does the State 2 security review’s dependency category cover every installed resolved distribution, or only the four direct pins named in deploy/requirements.txt?

quotes: - dependencies: APPLICABLE; references: A32; affected: deploy/requirements.txt (fastapi, pydantic, argon2-cffi, uvicorn pinned)

Before it,
   every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read in that

judgement.why: The security-review category resolves by reference to A32, whose affected set expressly includes both direct pins and every distribution resolved into the image; the requirements-file text identifies the direct-import area rather than narrowing A32.

topics.topic: Whether the wall-clock arithmetic prohibition permits deriving expiry as now plus TTL
questions: Does “no arithmetic” prohibit only adjusting the clock reading used as `now`, or does it also prohibit the explicitly required `now + TTL` expiry derivation?

quotes:
- the wall clock gives the instant: the current UTC time as an offset-naive
  datetime, one reading per operation for its own timestamps, the same value
  `datetime.utcnow()` gives (no cache, no local time, no second reading by
  the operation, no arithmetic); the audit writer's reading of an appended
  record's `occurred_at` is the one further reading (the exception above);

- CLK-001: all portal-owned event timestamps written by one operation, other than an

judgement.divergence: A staff-login implementation either adds the configured TTL to the one wall-clock instant and creates the prescribed expiry, or treats all arithmetic on that instant as forbidden and cannot create that expiry; the staff member and the CLK-001 verifier observe the difference.
judgement.why: The wall-clock passage forbids arithmetic without an exception, while CLK-001 expressly requires arithmetic on the same instant to derive TTL-based expiry.

topics.topic: Whether withdrawn affected-version OSV entries block deployment
questions: Does an affected-version entry marked withdrawn in the OSV data read for this deploy block the deploy?

quotes:
A distribution has a known vulnerability when an OSV entry that is not
   withdrawn lists its installed version as affected; reachability inside
   the portal is not judged case by case, so such a distribution blocks the
   deploy whatever feature the advisory concerns.
judgement.why: The normative definition expressly excludes withdrawn OSV entries, so an affected-version entry marked withdrawn does not constitute the known vulnerability forbidden by DEP-002.
